before: def first.note defines a singleton method on first, not an instance method for every Guide. Other Guide objects do not acquire it.
Inside class Guide, self is the class object. def self.kind defines a method called as Guide.kind, often called a class method. It is not called on Guide.new.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
class Guide
  def self.kind
    "study"
  end
end
first = Guide.new
second = Guide.new
def first.note
  "only first"
end
puts Guide.kind
puts first.note
```

Expected output or behavior: study
only first. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Second is another instance and does not get this method.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
class Guide
  def self.kind
    "study"
  end
end
first = Guide.new
second = Guide.new
def first.note
  "only first"
end
puts Guide.kind
puts first.note
```
The output is `study`, then `only first`. Kind belongs to the Guide class itself. Note belongs to first.
